title: Local food culture highlights
intro: Food spots tied to Singapore's everyday food culture: family-run stalls and long-standing makers behind dishes locals grew up with. We'll keep adding more.

items.name: New Horse Noodles
items.address: 335 Smith St, Chinatown Complex Food Centre #02-148 (Red Zone), Singapore 050335
items.story: Brothers Scott and Troy Lee left finance careers to open this Hakka yong tau foo stall, learning from an 85-year-old hawker in Malacca. Their handmade pieces come with Malaysian-style dark-sauce dry noodles. They have announced a final business day of 25 October 2026.
tips: Reported hours: Sat-Wed, 9:30am-2pm; closed Thu/Fri. The owners advise coming before 1pm. Check with the stall before travelling.
The S$6.50 noodle-and-yong-tau-foo set is the article-reported price, not a live menu quote.
Contains pork; the filling also includes seafood.

items.name: The Neighbourwok
items.address: 177 Bukit Batok West Ave 8, Get Together Coffeeshop, Singapore 650177
items.story: A coffeeshop stall in Bukit Batok known for wet-style Hokkien prawn mee. In the creator's video, a group shares a big plate with large prawns and each gives it an A or A+. The stall's own page lists its address as the Get Together Coffeeshop.
tips: The video is the creator's own taste test, so treat the grades as one group's opinion.
Check opening hours and queues with the stall before you travel.

items.name: Mr & Mrs Mohgan Super Crispy Roti Prata
items.address: 300 Joo Chiat Rd, Tin Yeang Restaurant, Singapore 427551
items.story: A prata couple known for crisp, thin prata with chicken curry, run from a stall inside Tin Yeang Restaurant. Time Out reported in 2019 that the Mohgans had run prata for over thirty years, first down the road at Crane Road.
tips: Listings show morning opening hours and a Wednesday closure. The video title says it sells out by noon, so go early and check before you travel.

video.title: I Finally Try Singapore's LEGENDARY Roti Prata (sold out by noon!)
video.author: Ghib Ojisan

items.name: Kway Guan Huat Joo Chiat Popiah
items.story: Popiah skin made the traditional way, by spreading dough on a hot pan in one smooth motion. The Straits Times reports the shop at 95 Joo Chiat Road was founded in 1938 and is now run by the third generation. The shop describes a family recipe from Fujian and offers popiah tours.
tips: The shophouse was rebuilt in a Peranakan style in 2018, according to the shop.
Check opening hours and tour bookings with the shop before you go.

note: Illustrations are concept art. The scenes, people and dishes are not photos of these shops or their food.
